note: Interpretive guide, one entry per provision ID in references/cra-requirements-catalog.generated.json. The verbatim legal text lives in the generated catalogue; this file says what evidence shows conformance, how to test, and what usually goes wrong. 'guidance' refers to Commission guidance C(2026) 5252 (non-binding); 'FAQ' to the Commission CRA FAQ (non-binding). Entries marked assessable=false are Commission powers or definitions and get status NOT_APPLICABLE in the matrix with the reason 'not a manufacturer obligation'.

AI.P1.1.title: Appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks
AI.P1.1.meaning: Umbrella requirement: all risks identified in the Article 13(2) risk assessment are treated, including any not covered by (2)(a) to (m). Fulfilled where all other applicable requirements are met and no identified risk is left untreated (guidance points 164 to 166).
evidence: risk assessment with full treatment of each identified risk
tests: sample threat scenarios and confirm measures exist and were verified
common_gaps: risks identified but no measure or justification
risk accepted on cost grounds (guidance point 163)

AI.P1.2.title: Chapeau: requirements (a) to (m) apply on the basis of the risk assessment and where applicable
AI.P1.2.meaning: Each of (a) to (m) is applicable unless the risk assessment justifies otherwise; justification goes into the technical documentation (Article 13(4)). Assess this item as the completeness of the applicability statements.
evidence: applicability and implementation statement for each of (a) to (m)
tests: check every letter has a decision and justification
guidance: FAQ 'Does a manufacturer need to implement all the essential requirements?'

AI.P1.2a.title: No known exploitable vulnerabilities at making available
AI.P1.2a.meaning: At placing on the market the product must not contain vulnerabilities that are known (public databases including the EU vulnerability database, disclosure to the manufacturer, own testing, prominent media) and exploitable under practical operational conditions. Risk-based judgement per vulnerability; document the exploitability analysis (guidance points 230 to 237).
evidence: SCA and SAST results for the released version
known-exploited-vulnerability cross-check (EUVD, CISA KEV, vendor advisories)
VEX or triage record for each unresolved component vulnerability with exploitability reasoning
tests: run SCA against the SBOM of the shipped version
verify reachability analysis for high-severity component vulnerabilities
check release process blocks known exploitable vulnerabilities
common_gaps: component vulnerabilities shipped without exploitability analysis
analysis done on a different version than shipped
guidance: FAQ 'How can a manufacturer ensure that a product is free from all vulnerabilities?'

AI.P1.2b.title: Secure by default configuration, with reset to original state
AI.P1.2b.meaning: Delivered configuration must be secure for the intended purpose: no default or shared credentials, unnecessary services and interfaces disabled, debug interfaces closed, secure protocol defaults, least-privilege defaults; the user can reset to that original state. Deviation only for tailor-made products under explicit agreement with a business user. A component is responsible only for the configuration it ships with.
evidence: service and port inventory in default state
tests: inspect factory or fresh-install state on a test unit
attempt to use documented default credentials
scan listening services in default state
common_gaps: insecure legacy protocols enabled by default for compatibility without risk justification
guidance: FAQ 'How does the secure-by-default requirement work?'

AI.P1.2c.title: Vulnerabilities addressable through security updates; automatic security updates where applicable, with opt-out, notification and postponement
AI.P1.2c.meaning: The product must be updatable for security. Where applicable (consumer products in particular), automatic security updates installed within an appropriate timeframe are enabled by default, with a clear easy opt-out, notification of available updates, and the option to postpone. Not applicable to products primarily intended for integration as components, or where users would not reasonably expect automatic updates such as professional, critical and industrial environments (Recital 56); notification and availability still apply.
evidence: opt-out and postponement UI or configuration
tests: observe update flow on a test unit: notification, default behaviour, opt-out, postpone
confirm security updates can be delivered separately (see AI.P2.2)
common_gaps: no update path at all for firmware
automatic updates off by default on consumer devices without justification
guidance: FAQ 'Is the manufacturer responsible for the installation of security updates by the product's users?'

AI.P1.2d.title: Protection from unauthorised access; reporting of possible unauthorised access
AI.P1.2d.meaning: Authentication, identity and access management appropriate to the risk, for all interfaces including local, network, remote data processing solutions and administrative paths; plus a mechanism to report possible unauthorised access (alerts, logs, notifications).
tests: two-identity authorisation tests on test resources
unauthenticated access attempts on every interface
verify unauthorised-access events are recorded or reported
common_gaps: missing authorisation checks on backend APIs
no detection or reporting of failed access

AI.P1.2e.title: Confidentiality of stored, transmitted and processed data
AI.P1.2e.meaning: State-of-the-art encryption at rest and in transit where relevant, plus other technical means, proportionate to the data and the risk. Relying on the platform's mature cryptography can be a valid design choice (guidance example 67).
evidence: data inventory with protection per store and channel
cryptographic configuration (algorithms, key sizes, key management)
tests: inspect data at rest on a test unit
common_gaps: cleartext local storage of secrets or personal data

AI.P1.2f.title: Integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration; reporting of corruption
AI.P1.2f.meaning: Protection against unauthorised manipulation of data, commands, software and configuration (signing, integrity checks, secure boot where appropriate, authenticated commands) and detection or reporting of corruption.
evidence: secure boot or integrity verification evidence
tests: attempt to install a modified update or configuration on a test unit
verify signature checks and failure reporting

AI.P1.2g.title: Data minimisation
AI.P1.2g.meaning: Process only data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the intended purpose, personal or otherwise. Overlaps with GDPR for personal data but applies to all data.
evidence: data inventory with purpose per data item
tests: review collected and transmitted data against purposes

AI.P1.2h.title: Availability of essential and basic functions, including after an incident; resilience against denial of service
AI.P1.2h.meaning: Essential and basic functions remain available or recover after incidents; resilience and mitigation against denial-of-service proportionate to the product (rate limiting, resource bounds, fail-safe states, recovery).
tests: bounded load or fault-injection tests in isolated environments with authorisation
recovery test on a test unit
common_gaps: no fail-safe state on backend loss
unbounded resource consumption on malformed input
guidance: C(2026) 5252 point 169 on outages of external services

AI.P1.2i.title: Minimise negative impact on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks
AI.P1.2i.meaning: The product must not become a source of harm to others: bandwidth abuse, amplification, botnet behaviour, network misbehaviour. Relevant for networked devices and software with network capabilities.
tests: observe traffic patterns and failure behaviour
common_gaps: no outbound restrictions on compromised devices

AI.P1.2j.title: Limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces
AI.P1.2j.meaning: Only necessary interfaces, services, ports, protocols and features exposed; unnecessary ones removed or disabled; hardened defaults for what remains.
evidence: interface and service inventory with justification
tests: port and interface scan on test unit
firmware and image analysis for unused services and tools
common_gaps: unused services compiled in and running

AI.P1.2k.title: Reduce the impact of an incident using exploitation mitigation mechanisms
AI.P1.2k.meaning: Exploit mitigations and containment proportionate to the platform: memory-safety protections (ASLR, stack protection, CFI where available), sandboxing and privilege separation, least privilege, isolation of components, secure coding practices.
evidence: secure coding standard and evidence of application
tests: review process privileges and isolation on a test unit
common_gaps: everything runs as root or administrator
no sandboxing of parsers of untrusted input

AI.P1.2l.title: Security-related logging and monitoring of relevant internal activity, with user opt-out
AI.P1.2l.meaning: Record and monitor security-relevant events including access to or modification of data, services or functions, in a way users can use; provide an opt-out for the user.
tests: generate security events on a test unit and confirm records
verify logs do not leak secrets
common_gaps: logs inaccessible to users or operators

AI.P1.2m.title: Secure and easy permanent removal of all data and settings; secure transfer where applicable
AI.P1.2m.meaning: Users can securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently (factory reset, account deletion, secure erase) and, where data can be transferred to other products or systems, do so securely.
tests: perform reset or deletion on test data and verify residual data on device and backend
common_gaps: reset leaves data on flash or in the cloud

AI.P2.1.title: Identify and document vulnerabilities and components, including an SBOM
AI.P2.1.meaning: Maintain a component inventory and a vulnerability register; produce an SBOM in a commonly used machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies for each product version. See references/sbom-standard.md.
evidence: SBOM per release validated by scripts/check_sbom.py
tests: reconcile SBOM with lockfiles and build

AI.P2.2.title: Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay in relation to the risks; security updates separate from functionality updates where technically feasible
AI.P2.2.meaning: Risk-based remediation with timelines; remedies may be patches, advisories with workarounds, configuration guidance or documentation depending on risk; security-only updates where feasible so users need not take feature updates to get fixes.
evidence: vulnerability response procedure with severity-based targets
documented cases where bundling was technically necessary
tests: trace sample vulnerabilities from intake to fix
check release channel supports security-only updates
common_gaps: security fixes only in major feature releases
component vulnerabilities not tracked to closure
guidance: FAQ 'Are manufacturers required to patch all vulnerabilities'
FAQ 'How should manufacturers ensure a separation between security and functionality updates'

AI.P2.3.title: Effective and regular tests and reviews of product security
AI.P2.3.meaning: Recurring and event-driven security testing proportionate to the risk profile: review whether new threats or vulnerabilities require new or updated tests and execute them; regression testing after changes (guidance points 238 to 240).
evidence: review records after new threats or vulnerabilities
tests: sample test records for the current version
common_gaps: no review trigger when new vulnerabilities appear
tests not covering the remote data processing solution

AI.P2.4.title: Share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities once a security update is available
AI.P2.4.meaning: Publish advisories with description, affected product identification, impact, severity and clear remediation guidance; justified delay allowed until users could patch.
tests: check advisories exist for past fixed vulnerabilities and contain required elements
common_gaps: advisories without affected versions or guidance

AI.P2.5.title: Policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure, put in place and enforced
AI.P2.5.meaning: A published CVD policy that is actually followed: intake, acknowledgement, triage, coordination, disclosure, safe harbour. See references/vulnerability-handling.md.
tests: send a labelled test report and observe handling
common_gaps: policy exists but reports go unanswered
no process for third-party component reports

AI.P2.6.title: Facilitate sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities, including a contact address
AI.P2.6.meaning: A working, published contact for vulnerability reports about the product and its third-party components; measures to share information (for example with CSIRTs, upstream maintainers and users).
evidence: contact listed in Annex II user information
tests: verify Annex II point 2 includes it
common_gaps: contact only in a web form behind login

AI.P2.7.title: Mechanisms to securely distribute updates, automatically where applicable for security updates
AI.P2.7.meaning: Update distribution with integrity and authenticity (signing), protected transport, verification on the product, resilience against downgrade where appropriate, and automation where applicable.
evidence: update channel design and key management
tests: apply legitimate and tampered updates on a test unit

AI.P2.8.title: Security updates disseminated without delay and free of charge, with advisory messages
AI.P2.8.meaning: Once available, security updates reach users promptly and free (except tailor-made products by agreement), accompanied by advisory messages with the relevant information and actions.
evidence: pricing or licence terms showing security updates are free
tests: review time from fix to availability
confirm no paywall for security updates
common_gaps: security updates gated behind support contracts for non-tailor-made products

AII.1.title: Manufacturer identity and contact details
AII.1.meaning: Name or trademark, postal address, email or other digital contact, website where available, in the user information.
common_gaps: only a web form, no postal address

AII.2.title: Single point of contact for vulnerability reports and location of the CVD policy
AII.2.meaning: The user information states where vulnerabilities can be reported and received and where the CVD policy is.

AII.3.title: Name, type and unique identification of the product
AII.3.meaning: Enough to identify the exact product and version.
common_gaps: version not identifiable by the user

AII.4.title: Intended purpose, security environment, essential functionalities and security properties
AII.4.meaning: The user information describes the intended purpose including the security environment provided by the manufacturer, the essential functions, and the security properties.
tests: consistency with risk assessment and marketing

AII.5.title: Known or foreseeable circumstances leading to significant cybersecurity risks
AII.5.meaning: Circumstances in intended use or reasonably foreseeable misuse that may cause significant risk, as identified in the risk assessment, are disclosed to users.
tests: compare with risk assessment residual risks
common_gaps: residual risks known internally but not disclosed

AII.6.title: Internet address of the EU declaration of conformity, where applicable
AII.6.meaning: Required where the declaration is provided online or a simplified declaration is used.

AII.7.title: Type of technical security support and end date of the support period
AII.7.meaning: What security support is offered and until when users can expect vulnerabilities handled and updates provided.
tests: consistency with Article 13(8) determination and 13(19) display

AII.8.title: Detailed instructions (or their internet address) on secure use

AII.8a.title: Measures during initial commissioning and throughout the lifetime to ensure secure use
AII.8a.meaning: Secure setup and ongoing operation guidance.
common_gaps: generic text not matched to the product

AII.8b.title: How changes to the product can affect the security of data
AII.8b.meaning: Explain how configuration changes, integrations or updates affect data security.

AII.8c.title: How security-relevant updates can be installed
tests: presence and accuracy against the update mechanism

AII.8d.title: Secure decommissioning, including secure removal of user data
AII.8d.meaning: How to decommission and remove data securely.

AII.8e.title: How to turn off the default automatic installation of security updates
AII.8e.meaning: Where automatic updates are enabled by default under Annex I Part I (2)(c), explain the opt-out.

AII.8f.title: Information for integrators, where the product is intended for integration
AII.8f.meaning: For components: information integrators need to meet Annex I and Annex VII for their products (security properties, configuration, update dependencies, support period).
common_gaps: component documentation silent on security and support

AII.9.title: Where the SBOM can be accessed, if the manufacturer makes it available to users
AII.9.meaning: Conditional: only if the manufacturer chooses to publish the SBOM.

AV.2.title: Declaration: manufacturer or authorised representative name and address

AV.4.title: Declaration: object of the declaration allowing traceability

AV.5.title: Declaration: statement of conformity with the relevant Union harmonisation legislation
AV.5.meaning: Single declaration where several Union acts apply (Article 28(3)).

AV.6.title: Declaration: references to harmonised standards, common specifications or certification
AV.6.meaning: Only standards actually cited in the OJEU and applied; otherwise none.
common_gaps: citing draft or uncited standards as harmonised

AV.7.title: Declaration: notified body, procedure and certificate where applicable

AV.8.title: Declaration: additional information, signature block
AV.8.meaning: Place and date, name, function, signature. The skill leaves this unsigned.

AVII.1c.title: Hardware: photographs or illustrations of external features, marking and internal layout

AVII.1d.title: User information and instructions as set out in Annex II

AVII.2.title: Design, development, production and vulnerability-handling description

AVII.2a.title: Design and development information including architecture and component interactions
tests: architecture explains how components build on each other

AVII.2b.title: Vulnerability-handling specifications: SBOM, CVD policy, contact address evidence, secure update distribution

AVII.2c.title: Production and monitoring processes and their validation
AVII.2c.meaning: Build, release and production controls, and how they are validated (reproducible builds, release gates, signing ceremonies, manufacturing test).

AVII.3.title: Cybersecurity risk assessment including applicability of Annex I Part I

AVII.4.title: Information taken into account to determine the support period

AVII.5.title: Harmonised standards, common specifications or certification schemes applied, or descriptions of solutions adopted and other specifications applied
AVII.5.meaning: With no cited harmonised standards, this item carries the per-requirement description of solutions and the other specifications used.
tests: every applicable requirement has a described solution
common_gaps: claims of harmonised standard use where none is cited

AVII.6.title: Reports of tests verifying conformity of the product and of the vulnerability-handling processes
AVII.6.meaning: For pre-CRA designs, current tests rather than historical design-phase tests are acceptable where the risk assessment supports it (guidance point 38).
tests: reports cover Parts I and II

AVII.7.title: Copy of the EU declaration of conformity
AVII.7.meaning: Draft until signed by the manufacturer.

AVII.8.title: SBOM on reasoned request from a market surveillance authority, where applicable

A13.1.title: Design, development and production in accordance with Annex I Part I
A13.1.meaning: Summary obligation evidenced by the Annex I Part I results and the development process.

A13.2.title: Undertake a cybersecurity risk assessment and take it into account across planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance
evidence: evidence it informed design and maintenance
common_gaps: assessment written after the fact with no design influence (acceptable for pre-CRA designs only with the guidance point 35 approach)

A13.3.title: Risk assessment documented, updated during the support period, with the required minimum content and the Annex I applicability statements

A13.4.title: Risk assessment included in technical documentation; justification for non-applicable requirements

A13.5.title: Due diligence when integrating third-party components, including non-commercial FOSS
A13.5.meaning: Proportionate verification that components do not compromise the product: conformity evidence or CE marking, update history, vulnerability database checks, additional tests (Recital 34); define what the product needs from each component and verify it (guidance section 7.3).

A13.6.title: Report component vulnerabilities upstream; remediate; share developed fixes

A13.7.title: Systematically document relevant cybersecurity aspects, including vulnerabilities and third-party information; update the risk assessment

A13.8.title: Handle vulnerabilities effectively for the support period; determine the support period per the criteria; minimum five years; document the determination; have CVD and vulnerability-processing procedures
common_gaps: five years declared by default without analysis

A13.9.title: Security updates remain available for at least 10 years after issue or the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer
common_gaps: updates removed when versions are retired

A13.10.title: Remediation only for the latest substantially modified version where users can upgrade free of charge and without additional costs
A13.10.meaning: Optional relief; if relied on, conditions must be met and documented; other Part II obligations continue for all versions.
common_gaps: older versions dropped although upgrade requires new hardware

A13.11.title: Public software archives with clear risk information
common_gaps: old versions downloadable with no warning

A13.12.title: Draw up technical documentation; carry out the conformity assessment; draw up the declaration and affix CE marking
A13.12.meaning: Readiness is assessed; the acts themselves are the manufacturer's.

A13.13.title: Keep technical documentation and declaration for 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer

A13.14.title: Procedures to keep series production in conformity; account for changes in process, design and standards

A13.15.title: Type, batch or serial number or other identification on the product, packaging or accompanying document

A13.16.title: Manufacturer name and contact details on the product, packaging or accompanying document, and in the user information

A13.17.title: Single point of contact for users, easily identifiable, in the user information, allowing the user's preferred means and not only automated tools

A13.18.title: Annex II information with the product, understandable, clear; kept available for 10 years or the support period; online information kept online
common_gaps: documentation removed when products are retired

A13.19.title: End date of the support period (month and year) at the time of purchase; end-of-support notification where technically feasible

A13.20.title: Copy of the EU declaration of conformity or simplified declaration with the exact internet address

A13.21.title: Immediate corrective measures, withdrawal or recall where non-conformity is known or suspected during the support period
guidance: FAQ 'Does the manufacturer need to recall the product'

A13.22.title: Provide information and documentation to market surveillance authorities on reasoned request; cooperate
tests: can the manufacturer produce the technical documentation on request

A13.23.title: Inform authorities and users before ceasing operations where obligations can no longer be met

A13.24.title: Commission power to specify SBOM format and elements
A13.24.meaning: Not a manufacturer obligation; check whether an implementing act exists.

A13.25.title: Union-wide dependency assessment; authorities may request SBOMs
A13.25.meaning: Not a manufacturer obligation beyond providing the SBOM on request.

A14.1.title: Notify actively exploited vulnerabilities to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA via the single reporting platform

A14.2.title: Early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within 14 days of a corrective measure

A14.3.title: Notify severe incidents having an impact on the security of the product
common_gaps: incident response not linked to CRA reporting

A14.4.title: Incident early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within one month of the notification

A14.5.title: Severity criteria for incidents
A14.5.meaning: Decision criteria must mirror Article 14(5)(a) and (b).
common_gaps: criteria based on business impact only

A14.7.title: Submission through the correct CSIRT endpoint: main establishment or the fallback order
common_gaps: non-EU manufacturer has not determined its CSIRT

A14.8.title: Inform impacted users (and where appropriate all users) of the vulnerability or incident and mitigations, where appropriate in machine-readable form
common_gaps: no customer contact data for devices sold through retail

A14.9.title: Commission delegated act on grounds for delaying dissemination
A14.9.meaning: Adopted as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/881; manufacturers may request delay and indicate sensitivity, deadlines unchanged.

A14.10.title: Commission implementing acts on notification format and procedures
A14.10.meaning: None identified as adopted; platform fields govern in practice.
